title: Prendre, venir, tenir et vouloir
summary: Switch stems correctly and transfer the pattern to useful verb families.
objectives: Conjugate all persons of prendre, venir, tenir and vouloir in the present subjunctive.
Apply family patterns to comprendre, apprendre, revenir and obtenir.

sections.title: Use prenn- or pren- according to the person
paragraphs: A stem is the part to which a person ending is attached. For prendre, the singular and ils/elles use prenn-; nous and vous use pren-. This resembles the indicative contrast ils prennent / nous prenons, but the subjunctive endings are still -e, -es, -e, -ions, -iez, -ent.

Keep a derivative's prefix: comprendre gives comprenne, comprennes, comprenne, comprenions, compreniez, comprennent; apprendre gives apprenne, apprennes, apprenne, apprenions, appreniez, apprennent. The same transfer works for reprendre and surprendre.
points: The double n belongs only to the prenn- group.

examples.french:
que je **prenne**
que tu **prennes**
qu'il/elle/on **prenne**
que nous **prenions**
que vous **preniez**
qu'ils/elles **prennent**
examples.english:
that I take
that you take
that he/she/one take
that we take
that you take
that they take
examples.note: All six persons are needed to see both stems.

examples.french: Il faut que nous **comprenions** le problème.
examples.english: We need to understand the problem.
She needs to learn to delegate.

mistakes.avoid: Il faut que vous prenniez le train.
mistakes.prefer: Il faut que vous preniez le train.
mistakes.why: Nous and vous use pren-, with one n.

sections.title: Vienn-/ven- and tienn-/ten-
paragraphs: Venir and tenir have parallel stem changes. The singular and ils/elles use vienn- and tienn-; nous and vous use ven- and ten-. Their derivatives keep the prefix and the same six-person pattern.

Revenir: revienne, reviennes, revienne, revenions, reveniez, reviennent. Obtenir: obtienne, obtiennes, obtienne, obtenions, obteniez, obtiennent. Devenir, intervenir, retenir and maintenir work in the same way with their own prefixes.

examples.french:
que je **vienne**
que tu **viennes**
qu'il/elle/on **vienne**
que nous **venions**
que vous **veniez**
qu'ils/elles **viennent**
examples.english:
that I come
that you come
that he/she/one come
that we come
that you come
that they come
examples.note: Do not import the future stem viendr-.

examples.french:
que je **tienne**
que tu **tiennes**
qu'il/elle/on **tienne**
que nous **tenions**
que vous **teniez**
qu'ils/elles **tiennent**
examples.english:
that I hold
that you hold
that he/she/one hold
that we hold
that you hold
that they hold
examples.note: Tenir can also mean keep, as in keep a promise.

examples.english: You need to come back on Friday.
examples.note: The prefix re- does not change the pattern.

examples.french: Il faut qu'ils **obtiennent** un accord écrit.
examples.english: They need to obtain a written agreement.

examples.french: Il faut que nous **tenions** notre promesse.
examples.english: We need to keep our promise.

mistakes.why: The nous stem is ven-, not vienn-.

sections.title: Vouloir has its own two-stem pattern
paragraphs: Vouloir uses veuill- in the singular and ils/elles, but voul- for nous and vous. These forms can follow a construction requiring the subjunctive, such as bien que (although). Separately, an indicative vouloir in a main clause can itself select a subjunctive after que: je veux que tu viennes. The first verb does not automatically become subjunctive just because the second one is.

examples.french:
que je **veuille**
que tu **veuilles**
qu'il/elle/on **veuille**
que nous **voulions**
que vous **vouliez**
qu'ils/elles **veuillent**
examples.english:
that I want
that you want
that he/she/one want
that we want
that you want
that they want
examples.note: The ll of veuill- does not survive in voulions.

examples.french: Bien que nous **voulions** aider, nous manquons de temps.
examples.english: Although we want to help, we are short of time.
examples.note: A real wish appears in the subjunctive after bien que.

examples.french: Bien qu'elle **veuille** rester, elle doit partir.
examples.english: Although she wants to stay, she has to leave.
examples.note: Present subjunctive, not veillera or voudra.

practice.prompt: Present subjunctive of prendre only: Il faut que tu ___ des notes.
Present subjunctive of venir only: Il faut que vous ___ ensemble.
Present subjunctive of tenir only: Il faut qu'elle ___ la porte.
Supply vouloir in the present subjunctive: Bien qu'ils ___ participer, ils sont absents.
Supply comprendre in the present subjunctive: Il faut que vous ___ ce risque.
Supply apprendre in the present subjunctive: Il faut qu'ils ___ le code.
Supply obtenir in the present subjunctive: Il faut que nous ___ une réponse.
Supply revenir in the present subjunctive: Il faut qu'il ___ avant la nuit.
Supply vouloir in the present subjunctive: Bien que vous ___ continuer, la séance est terminée.
Supply vouloir in the present subjunctive: Bien que je ___ économiser, je dois acheter un vélo.
Supply maintenir in the present subjunctive: Il faut que tu ___ le contact.
practice.explanation: Maintain the prefix main- and the tienn- stem.

practice.prompt: Supply reprendre in the present subjunctive: Il faut que nous ___ la discussion.
Supply devenir in the present subjunctive: Il faut que cette information ___ publique.
Supply surprendre in the present subjunctive: Il faut que le spectacle ___ le public.
Supply vouloir in the present subjunctive: Bien que tu ___ partir, attends cinq minutes.
Supply retenir in the present subjunctive: Il faut que vous ___ ces trois dates.

production_task.prompt: Organize a volunteer handover. Write three requirements using a prendre-family verb, a venir-family verb and a tenir-family verb, plus one concession beginning bien que with vouloir.
production_task.model_answer: Il faut que les nouveaux bénévoles comprennent la procédure. Il faut que nous revenions demain. Il faut que chacun retienne le numéro d'urgence. Bien que nous voulions tout expliquer ce soir, il est déjà tard.
production_task.translation: The new volunteers need to understand the procedure. We need to come back tomorrow. Everyone needs to remember the emergency number. Although we want to explain everything this evening, it is already late.
rubric: The four target families are represented.
Nous/vous forms do not copy the singular stems.
The concession contrasts two compatible facts.
The handover instructions are specific and useful.
